item.title: Great Stuff.
item.content:encoded: I very rarely post anything here, but this may possibly be my favorite series of tales yet. It was the Wondertainment stuff and I honestly didn't think anything would top that, but alas, here we are/were/will be. It would've been so easy for this piece to become a jumbled mess but I feel like the writing and attention to detail was superb. Heartfelt kudos to the author. I understand these can't be easy to write and certainly a project like this takes time and effort, but should I be concerned about this being finished? Not wanting to complain or anything like that, I legitimately don't know if 8+ months means the author has moved on or not. Regardless, this whole thing was a joy to read. Thank you.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Interesting. I was just talking about time fuckery the other day. I choose to assume cause.

I can't fully explain why these kinds of tales succeed where a lot of others don't in taking a complex subject that could easily become way too convoluted for its own good and presenting it in an interesting manner. This is also a somewhat rare example of a conversation being meaty enough to merit a tale. Enjoyable, in any event.

If I have one observation, there's flashes here and there of a more literary style than the rest of the tale, namely the semi-narrative asides and the line where Xyank downs his drink. It's not a problem at all here, but I did find myself kind of wanting you to let that element off the chain a little more. Not that the other portions were too dry for my liking, but it was an interesting sensibility that I wouldn't mind seeing more of as this continues to develop.
